Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D3 supplementation did not change self-rated depression (BDI-II) scores compared with placebo.
Sentence: "Although the intervention led to a higher increase of 25(OH)D levels in the VG than in the PG (treatment difference: + 14 ng/ml; 95% CI 4.86-23.77; p = 0.003), the change in BDI-II scores did not differ (+ 1.3; 95% CI - 2.22 to 4.81; p = 0.466)."
Measured as: BDI-II score
Population: Child and adolescent psychiatric patients with vitamin D deficiency (25(OH)D ≤ 30 nmol/l) and at least mild depression (BDI-II > 13)
Intervention: Vitamin D3 2640 IU/day for 28 days plus treatment as usual
Comparator: Placebo plus treatment as usual
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 113
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation reduced depression severity (BDI-II) more than placebo in patients with mild to moderate depression.
Sentence: "At the end point, statistically significant changes were observed only in intervention group as compared with controls including increased 25(OH)D concentration (+ 40.83 ± 28.57 vs. + 5.14 ± 23.44 nmol L-1, P < 0.001) and decreased depression severity (-11.75 ± 6.40 vs. -3.61 ± 10.40, P = 0.003)."
Measured as: depression severity (Beck Depression Inventory-II)
Population: 56 patients aged 18-60 years with mild to moderate depression
Intervention: cholecalciferol 50,000 IU every 2 weeks for 8 weeks
Comparator: placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 56
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
